articles.title: Doomsday's Biggest Criticism Is Even Truer After the New Trailer & Highlights Why the Multiverse Saga Failed

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters in just a few weeks, and although anticipation is growing within the fanbase, the release of the final trailer has some concerned about a major issue with the plot. Yesterday's trailer came with a whole host of reveals, including, among other things, that Steve Rogers and Peggy Carter have son (who looks to be about pre-teen age, but that's not been clarified yet), that Steve and Bucky will finally be reunited , and seemingly that the theory that Steve is really Loki is wrong .

If that's sound like a lot of Steve Rogers, that's because it is. A surprising amount of the trailer was focused on Steve, which comes on the heels of Steve's Doomsday arc being teased in the bonus footage of Avengers: Endgame Encore , with Loki showing up to Steve and Peggy's house, likely to address the fact that Steve's decision to stay in the past and live out a married life with Peggy was the cause of Doomsday . Yet, some fans are taking significant issue with this emphasis on Steve, and it extends beyond just Doomsday , into a reflection of the Multiverse Saga as a whole.

Steve Rogers Was Absent in the Multiverse Saga, And Now He's a Central Figure If you felt very little (or perhaps nothing) with the reveal of Steve Rogers' son in the most recent Doomsday trailer, you wouldn't be alone, and that doesn't necessarily have anything to do with the frustrations over Steve's actions apparently causing Doomsday . Rather, it's simply difficult to feel emotionally affected by a reveal such as this one, considering that Steve hasn't been in an MCU project since Endgame seven years ago. With so much time away, audiences just may not have that same emotional investment, and that spells larger trouble because it seems as though Doomsday will be centering Steve as the emotional core of the movie. Yet, audiences are asking how that can be true when he hasn't even been around in years.

That is my problem with it https://t.co/FFEHn8NKDP

Presumably, Marvel wanted the return of Chris Evans/Steve Rogers to feel like a momentous occasion and, when it was first announced, a massive reveal, and perhaps that necessitated Steve not appearing at any point the Multiverse Saga. The trouble is that this gives Steve loose connections at best to what is happening, and that only reinforces the concerns that many fans had about Doomsday feeling disjointed or out of left field (something that also seems troubling in light of Thor's unfortunate line in the final Doomsday trailer , in which he admits he doesn't know half of the heroes present or what they do).

Now the question simply remains: can Doomsday effectively get audiences reinvested in Steve's story quickly enough to make the movie work? If the movie is only banking on viewers still caring about Steve from Endgame and earlier, it might find itself in some hot water. For now, audiences just have to wait and see.

Are you invested in Steve's story in Doomsday , or do you wish the focus was somewhere else? Let us know in the comment down below.

The Social Network and Fight Club filmmaker says he was approached to creatively lead big-budget The Lord of the Rings prequel series — and turned it down.

articles.title: One Hunger Games Star Turned Down Their Role Multiple Times: “I Didn't Think There Was Enough To Do”
articles.summary: Woody Harrelson turned down the role of Haymitch Abernathy in The Hunger Games twice before director Gary Ross convinced him to take the part. The actor had read Suzanne Collins’ books and liked them but wasn't convinced there was enough for him to do as Katniss Everdeen’s mentor. Fourteen years later, Harrelson is watching another […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Woody Harrelson turned down the role of Haymitch Abernathy in The Hunger Games twice before director Gary Ross convinced him to take the part. The actor had read Suzanne Collins’ books and liked them but wasn't convinced there was enough for him to do as Katniss Everdeen’s mentor. Fourteen years later, Harrelson is watching another actor take on the role of Haymitch in a movie built entirely around the character, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping .

Harrelson discussed his initial reservations about joining the franchise in a conversation with his successor, Joseph Zada, for Vanity Fair . "I thought it was good, I read the books, really good, but I just don’t think there’s enough to do. I don’t know if there’s enough to do. It’s an arbitrary, odd way of assessing it." The actor admitted that he can't imagine his life without the experience of making the movies and the friendships he formed along the way. Fortunately, Ross wasn't willing to take no for an answer. The director told Harrelson that he didn't have a second choice for Haymitch. After about ten minutes on the phone with Ross, Harrelson agreed to do the movie. He said, "Gary calls me, and he's like, 'Woody, you have to do this part. I don't have a second choice. You have to play Haymitch.’ And he just talked to me for about 10 minutes on the phone. I'm like, 'All right, okay, yeah, let's do it.'"

Harrelson has seen what Zada does with the character in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping and couldn't be happier with his successor. “I really can't imagine anyone doing a better job,” Harrelson told the young actor. He was particularly impressed with how Zada develops the cynicism that would come to define Haymitch. While audiences were introduced to the character as a hard-drinking, cynical mentor to Katniss and Peeta, Zada has the opportunity to show audiences the young man Haymitch was before the Capitol robbed him of his optimism.

It's somewhat ironic that Harrelson was initially concerned about the size of the role given how much of the larger story of The Hunger Games hinges on Haymitch. He's one of the few characters who understands what Katniss is going through long before she becomes the face of the rebellion. Having survived the Second Quarter Quell , Haymitch knows that winning the Hunger Games doesn't necessarily mean you've beaten the Capitol. That informed Harrelson's performance across four movies, but audiences are only now getting to see how Haymitch learned that lesson.

Haymitch isn't even the only franchise mentor Harrelson has turned down twice. The actor was equally reluctant to play Tobias Beckett, Han Solo's mentor in Solo: A Star Wars Story . In that instance, it was producer Allison Shearmur who convinced Harrelson to take the role. Unfortunately, not every filmmaker has been as persistent with Harrelson as Ross and Shearmur were. Among the roles the actor has expressed regret over passing on are the title character in Jerry Maguire and Harry Dunne in Dumb and Dumber . Harrelson famously told producer James L. Brooks that nobody was going to care about a movie about a sports agent. The role earned Tom Cruise his second Academy Award nomination.

What's remarkable about Collins' Sunrise on the Reaping is how much of the young Haymitch she introduces in the book feels consistent with Harrelson's interpretation of the character. Even without knowing the full extent of Haymitch's history, Harrelson always managed to convey how much the man cared about the kids he was being asked to send to their deaths. Now, thanks to Collins and Zada, audiences have a much better understanding of why. For a character Harrelson initially thought didn't have enough to do, Haymitch has proven to be one of the richest characters in the entire franchise. What role that he passed on do you wish Harrelson had taken? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: World of Warcraft: Forever's Success Is Staggering, But It Comes With The Same Catches As The Original
articles.summary: Courtesy of Blizzard World of Warcraft: Forever launched in early November 2026 and broke tons of Blizzard records in the process, but the game is starting to run into issues players can't ignore. This MMORPG is an alternate version of the original World of Warcraft, bringing back the original 2004 classic in a way that World of Warcraft: […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google World of Warcraft: Forever launched in early November 2026 and broke tons of Blizzard records in the process, but the game is starting to run into issues players can't ignore. This MMORPG is an alternate version of the original World of Warcraft , bringing back the original 2004 classic in a way that World of Warcraft: Classic doesn't. Separate from the modern versions of what WoW is turning into, yet still included in existing subscriptions to the current game, this redesigned title returns players to a nostalgic gameplay setting, but with all of the same pitfalls of that original design as well.

Some players have realized that World of Warcraft: Forever is more like an expansion to the original than a full redux of the first game, giving players a sandbox much closer to the launch of the original WoW . New zones, raids, races, abilities, combinations, build strategies, and more are available in WoW: Forever , but the game keeps the first WoW MMO's original Level 60 cap among other features exclusive to that version. Now that the game has been out for awhile, players are starting to have strong opinions about balancing, exploits, and other features veteran fans might remember were pivotal talking points of the classic World of Warcraft .

Around 15 million or more characters have been made in World of Warcraft: Forever , within less than a month of the title's release. Currently, WoW: Forever has more players than World of Warcraft has had in the last 15 years, with a higher count of characters than the MMO has kept in a long time. Before this, WoW: Cataclysm was the biggest expansion for the game, but Forever 's numbers are actually closer to the first World of Warcraft 's launch than anything else. The momentum of this game can't be denied, with so many players returning to the world of Azeroth or jumping into it for the first time.

Some of the biggest praise for WoW: Forever comes from the game's classic MMO design, where players are given more opportunities to encounter quests through non-linear exploration. Rather than being funneled into linear questlines and scripted segments, players have a greater amount of goals to pursue based on their curiosity. Instead of the game telling you what to do and where to go, characters can party up and simply gain 10-15 quests at a rapid pace just by interacting with the world. More interesting decision making helps elevate the World of Warcraft: Forever experience, but it isn't without its flaws.

With such an authentic return to form of the original WoW design comes the same problems that forced that game to evolve. Currently, one such problem is the multiple infinite money glitches that players are exploiting to bypass progression and trade, with some players running around with endless cash. Clearing some non-elite enemies in the same location over and over would allow players to loot upwards to 100 raw Gold per hour, farming it endlessly to fetch a king's ransom. While Blizzard has issued bans and trade blocks to certain accounts as a result, these exploits mirror WoW 's issues from back in the early 2000s.

Tedium is also a huge enemy of players in World of Warcraft: Forever , as nostalgic design also brings back less fondly remembered grinding for levels, gear, and other content. Poorly itemized gear was vanilla WoW 's kryptonite at times, along with balancing issues that made class synergy for PvP unbearable. To that point, WoW: Forever has several balance problems as of this time of writing too, such as the underwhelming lack of strength given to certain classes. The Holy Paladin and healer specs from other archetypes are severely handicapped right now, with healing builds struggling to keep up.

Currently, Blizzard has very few solutions to any of these systemic issues in World of Warcraft: Forever , instead just handing out bans and telling players to pick different builds rather than addressing issues directly. This could be just a problem in timing, as the game is still within its first month of launch, and sweeping balance updates and other changes take time to implement. However, veteran players worry that Blizzard's slow response time to make changes might lead to increasing friction and frustrating in WoW: Forever , causing players to log off. Right now, some of the biggest issues players want addressed fast are:

Should this game sit within the same problems that plagued the 2004 title that took the world by storm, it may suffer a similar fate. Hardcore classic players will always appreciate the oldest version of the MMO, but nostalgia shouldn't blind fans to much-needed changes Blizzard could implement quickly with modern resources. For World of Warcraft: Forever to even surpass the appeal of the original WoW , it will have to tackle problems head-on, using 22 years of hindsight as a guiding light to help players who want the best experience possible.

What kind of changes would you make to World of Warcraft: Forever right now? Let us know in the comments below!

Three friends from India take on one of the most remote roads on the planet in "Carretera Austral – A Journey to the End of the World," a fiction feature that Mumbai-based Spherecho Productions plans to shoot in southern Chile with help from Chilean outfit Praxia Producciones.

The two companies signed a letter of intent at the WAVES Film Bazaar , the market component of the International Film Festival of India in Goa. Praxia, headquartered in the southern Chilean town of Puerto Varas, was represented by founder Amanda Puga Salman. Ranaksh Rana represented Spherecho. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories CMA Awards See a 55% Ratings Bump in Key Adult Demo With Taylor Swift's Return to the Show Taylor Swift Ties Grammy Record for Consecutive Album of the Year Nominations

The Carretera Austral, or Route 7, winds south through Chilean Patagonia, and the letter bills it as "the loneliest road in the world." The trio's journey takes them farther and farther from the rest of the world, and in the process they come closer to who they really are. Megha Das, who also goes by Megha Rana and is a member of India's Screenwriters Association, wrote the script. The title is tentative.

articles.title: Thanksgiving Box Office: 'Focker In-Law' and Disney's 'Hexed' Vie for No. 2 Behind 'Sunrise on the Reaping'
articles.summary: Movie theater owners are hoping for a Thanksgiving box office feast. articles.content:
Movie theater owners are hoping for a Thanksgiving box office feast.

Lionsgate's " The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping " is poised to dominate over the holiday with projections of $80 million to $90 million between Wednesday and Sunday. That's after the dystopian prequel launched last weekend to $120 million, registering as the fifth-largest domestic debut of the year. "Sunrise on the Reaping" will tower over two newcomers, Universal's family comedy "Focker In-Law" and Disney's animated " Hexed ," each of which land in roughly 3,500 theaters on Wednesday and are aiming for $40 million to $45 million over the five-day frame. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Taylor Swift's CMA Return Helped Disney Sell More Ads Taylor Swift Ties Grammy Record for Consecutive Album of the Year Nominations

Meanwhile, the Angel Studios biopic "Hershey," about the foundation of the chocolate empire, is projecting a $6 million to $8 million start over four days and Netflix's Brad Pitt-led "The Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth," a sequel to Sony's "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood," is targeting single digits from 250 Imax screens in North America.

This crop of offerings won't establish a Thanksgiving box office benchmark, though cinema operators are encouraged by the range of offerings. (Plus, domestic ticket sales are already 20% above the same point in 2025 as the box office prepares to surpass $10 billion for the first time since Covid upended the theatrical business). Thanksgiving 2024 was the holiday's biggest on record with $422 million across all films, led by "Moana 2″ ($225 million debut), “Wicked” ($118 million) and “Gladiator II” ($44 million). Other top Turkey Days were 2018 with $315 million, fueled by “Ralph Breaks the Internet,” “Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald” and “Creed II," 2014 with $294 million, powered by “The Hunger Games: Catching Fire," and 2025 with $293 million, boosted by "Zootopia 2" and "Wicked: For Good." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"Hexed" cost above $200 million to produce, not including the many millions spent on global marketing efforts. Since theater owners keep roughly half of ticket sales, Disney needs "Hexed" to resonate outside of the U.S. — and through the holiday season — to justify the massive price tag. While Disney's animated sequels like "Moana 2" and "Zootopia 2" are among the biggest Thanksgiving releases of all time, the studio has struggled with original fare, such as 2024's "Wish" ($31 million over its first five days) and 2022's "Strange World" ($18 million debut over its first five days). Word of mouth will factor into the box office longevity of "Hexed," which follows a teen girl who discovers magical powers that take her from suburbia to Hexe, the world of witches.

"Focker-In-Law" was made for $90 million, a substantial budget given the reality that comedies are a theatrical rarity. (Universal and Paramount co-financed the film.) However, the studios were willing to spend because the three prior films in the "Focker" universe were major box office winners. "Meet the Parents," which debuted 26 years ago and starred Ben Stiller and Robert De Niro as mismatched in-laws Greg Focker and Jack Byrnes, generated $330 million worldwide and inspired two commercially successful sequels, 2004’s “Meet the Fockers” ($522 million worldwide) and 2010’s “Little Fockers" ($310 million worldwide).

In the original, Stiller plays a hapless nurse who endures all kinds of chaos when he's introduced to his girlfriend's family. This time around, Stiller's Greg Focker is the patriarch as his son brings home a new no-nonsense girlfriend, portrayed by Ariana Grande. If "Focker-In-Law" exceeds theatrical expectations, Grande could cement herself as queen of the Thanksgiving box office. This is her third consecutive Turkey Day release following 2024's "Wicked" and 2025's "Wicked: For Good."

articles.title: We Already Know What Marvel's Ghost Rider Sequel Should Be, And It's a Major MCU Crossover
articles.summary: Spider-Man: Brand New Day proved that Marvel doesn’t need to gather the Avengers to stage a major crossover. Spider-Man, the Hulk, and the Punisher all brought three very different superhero archetypes together in one movie. With Ryan Gosling’s Ghost Rider coming in 2028, Marvel already has another unlikely trio from the comics waiting for a […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Spider-Man: Brand New Day proved that Marvel doesn’t need to gather the Avengers to stage a major crossover. Spider-Man, the Hulk, and the Punisher all brought three very different superhero archetypes together in one movie. With Ryan Gosling’s Ghost Rider coming in 2028, Marvel already has another unlikely trio from the comics waiting for a supernatural team-up on screen. The Spirit of Vengeance has a long road to hell ahead of him, but one of his adventures should unite three of Marvel’s most violent antiheroes.

Blackheart is the demon son of Mephisto and is an obvious villain for a Ghost Rider film. His daddy issues were on full display in Nicolas Cage's version when Wes Bentley portrayed the hellspawn. He’s basically the Loki of the Marvel supernatural universe, whose ambitions often bring together heroes to oppose him. With all of the Ghost Rider villains we haven't seen on screen, save Blackheart for the sequel this time around. And let Wolverine and Jon Bernthal’s Punisher come along for the ride. That’s the premise of 1991’s Ghost Rider/Wolverine/Punisher: Hearts of Darkness , a crossover that could give Marvel its next big team-up movie outside the Avengers.

In 1988, Marvel began publishing Marvel Comics Presents , a biweekly anthology that included original adventures outside of the characters' regular titles. Wolverine was practically its mascot, appearing in over 100 straight issues. That included Barry Windsor-Smith’s Weapon X in #72-84, which showed the horrific experiments that bonded adamantium to Logan’s skeleton. Then Ghost Rider joined the party. The #90 issue started the anthology as a flipbook, Wolverine on one cover and Ghost Rider on the other. In issue #100, they teamed up with Doctor Doom to battle Nightmare. The Punisher also showed up in a few issues, including #59 and #101.

Writer Howard Mackie and artist John Romita Jr. united the trio in 1991 for Hearts of Darkness . The oversized comic features Danny Ketch, Logan, and Frank Castle heading to Christ's Crown, a small town under the influence of Blackheart. He has promised each of them information they desperately want, but the demon has another offer. He needs their help to overthrow his father, Mephisto.

Blackheart believes he has three ready accomplices. Wolverine wrestles with his killer instincts. For Frank Castle, killing criminals is his life’s work. Ghost Rider literally rides around and punishes sinners. They're not exactly Boy Scouts, and Blackheart thinks he can use their violent tendencies to his own ends. When they refuse his offer, he takes a young girl named Lucy hostage, forcing the three into a confrontation that ends with Mephisto stepping in.

Blackheart was created by Romita Jr. and Ann Nocenti in Daredevil #270, two years before Hearts of Darkness . The crossover led to a sequel, 1994's The Dark Design , written by Mackie with art by Ron Garney. Back in Christ's Crown, Blackheart returns with an army of corrupted townspeople, forcing Ghost Rider, Wolverine, and the Punisher to team up once more to protect Lucy. The demon kills Mephisto and takes the throne of Hell. Children can be very ungrateful.

From the first time he brought the Avengers together in both the comics and films, Loki has been causing problems that have forced multiple superheroes to come together to stop his machinations. Blackheart could fill a similar role for Marvel’s supernatural characters. He’s strong enough to face off against Ghost Rider, manipulative enough to take advantage of Wolverine, and ambitious enough to threaten Mephisto himself. His schemes give heroes who would otherwise have no reason to work together a reason to do so. Instead of a one-and-done enemy, Blackheart could be a recurring antagonist and return with ever more ambitious schemes, throwing different combinations of Marvel characters into unlikely alliances. The Dark Design could be the supernatural MCU's Infinity War , with Blackheart succeeding in overthrowing his father.

Brand New Day showed what a blast these smaller crossovers could be. We could have Wolverine and The Punisher in Ghost Rider’s world, and it wouldn’t detract from Ghost Rider’s movie. Hulk and Punisher shared Spider-Man’s adventure. Christ’s Crown isn’t your usual MCU battleground, it’s got demons, possessed townsfolk, and three heroes who’d probably rather fight alone. Marvel has spent decades pairing unlikely characters to take on Blackheart . Hearts of Darkness offers a ready-made Ghost Rider sequel and a way to make the villain a recurring threat throughout the supernatural MCU.

Also, Ghost Rider and Wolverine already ride motorcycles. And if Jeremy Allen White ends up being Wolverine , we know he can handle a bike. Dolph Lundgren's Frank Castle rode one. Let's see if Jon Bernthal can handle a chopper too. What would these three even name their motorcycle club? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: Jason Segel Boards 'Meeting Your Maker,' Short About a Suicidal TV Puppet, as Executive Producer (Exclusive)
articles.summary: Written and directed by Gregory J.M. Kasunich, the Oscar-qualified dark comedy short stars Jonathan Kite ('2 Broke Girls') and Otis, a depressed kids' TV puppet star who must confront his creator.
articles.content:
Jason Segel ( Shrinking , The Muppets , Forgetting Sarah Marshall ) has joined the Oscar-qualified short film Meeting Your Maker as an executive producer. Written and directed by Gregory J.M. Kasunich, the heartfelt 18-minute dark comedy film follows Otis, a beloved children’s TV puppet who, following a suicide attempt, awakens in a workshop and must confront his creator. Otis must grapple with questions of identity, purpose, and what it means to be alive. The film stars Jonathan Kite ( 2 Broke Girls ) alongside Thomas Lennon, Amanda Maddock, Jason and Randy Sklar, Lenny Jacobson, Anna Chazelle, Kayla Radomski, Dylan Playfair, Dylan Mooney, Victor Yerrid and Darcy Rose Byrnes. The 18-minute short was produced by Derek Tramont and Lee Sacks. Segel has explored similar emotional territory throughout his career, from his work writing and starring in The Muppets to his performance in the Apple TV+ hit series Shrinking . Related Stories Movies How Iran's Pegah Ahangarani Turned Her Family Archives Into a Regime-Challenging Oscar Hopeful Movies Record Number of International and Animated Features Oscar-Eligible This Season

Blending practical puppetry, surreal production design, and an ensemble of comedic performers, Meeting Your Maker explores the complicated relationship between artists and their creations, asking what happens when the character you’ve spent your life bringing to life begins to question their own existence.

"There’s something really special about Meeting Your Maker ," said Segel. "It has this wonderful balance of comedy and heartbreak, this sort of magical melancholy that I’ve always been drawn to. It makes you laugh, and then, almost without realizing it, you find yourself thinking about some pretty big questions like who we are, what gives our lives meaning, and what happens when we lose sight of our purpose." Added Segel: "I’ve always believed that puppetry has this incredible ability to make us feel things we might otherwise be afraid to confront. There’s something about that innocence and imagination that allows us to be a little more honest with ourselves. And I think that’s especially important right now, when so many people are struggling to feel seen or connected. What Gregory has created is funny, strange, and ultimately hopeful. It reminds us that even in our darkest moments, there’s still room for laughter, connection, and magic. I was really moved by it, and I’m proud to come aboard as an executive producer." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

articles.title: I Wondered Why Marvel Dropped Those Four Avengers: Doomsday Teasers So Early. Joe Russo Explained
articles.summary: Those clips came surprisingly early.
articles.content:
Fans who spent years watching the Marvel movies in order are gearing up for the shared universe's next big crossover event with Avengers: Doomsday . Arguably the most anticipated upcoming Marvel movie in years, the blockbuster has been steadily building excitement since those teasers arrived back in January . Now Joe Russo explained why they decided to give us footage that early.

Marvel is known for its tight security , so it was surprising that we got footage from Doomsday so many months before the movie's December release. The industry has changed a bit since Endgame arrived in theaters, and the MCU has had a number of box office blunders including bombs like The Marvels . As such, The Russos wanted get the hype train running early, with more news, casting, and footage methodically released to the public.

Those brief clips quickly went viral, especially the Captain America teaser that confirmed Chris Evans was returning as Steve Rogers. With the next Avengers movie now just a few weeks away from its release, anticipation has reached a fever pitch that should (hopefully) result in massive box office numbers. Perhaps future MCU projects will follow this same strategy.

articles.content:
Chilean filmmaker Jorge López Sotomayor and Indian production company Pantellisense have signed a letter of intent to co-produce "The Fragile Empire of Ice," a feature that the partners plan to open up from Antarctica to the Arctic and the Himalayas.

The agreement was signed at the WAVES Film Bazaar , the market component of the International Film Festival of India in Goa. López Sotomayor, a director and producer, signed for himself and his banner JL Producciones. Pantellisense, based in Shimla in the northern Indian state of Himachal Pradesh, produces under the Two for Joy brand and was represented by founder and CEO Paras Prakash. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories CMAs Photo Gallery: See Taylor Swift, Ella Langley, Kacey Musgraves, Lainey Wilson, Stella Lefty and Other Stars on the Carpet and On-Stage Taylor Swift, Jaafar Jackson, ‘The Odyssey’ Among Hollywood Music in Media Awards Winners

The film adapts "Conquistadores de la Antártica" by Chilean writer Francisco Coloane. López Sotomayor co-wrote the screenplay, now in its fourth version, with Matías Villa Prieto, and a teaser and a storyboard graphic novel have already been made. JL Producciones originated the project.

The new framing treats the Himalayas as the "Third Pole." Outside the Arctic and Antarctic, the region holds more ice than anywhere else on Earth, and its rivers support close to 2 billion people. Under the letter, the two sides will rework the script together so the story moves beyond the South Pole and shows how the forces endangering Antarctica also put the Arctic and the glaciers of the Himalaya at risk. Changes could bring in Indian characters, for example a glaciologist with experience in both the Arctic and the Himalaya, along with scenes in those regions and Indian music and cultural elements. Those additions would help the film meet co-production requirements and connect with audiences in India. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The partners intend the project to be an official India- Chile co-production once the two governments have an audiovisual co-production agreement in place. That treaty is not yet in force. Chile's trade commissioner to India, Jorge Loyola, recently told Variety it had reached its final stage of negotiation. In the meantime, the letter allows for a contractual co-production or a structure involving a third country with treaties covering both India and Chile.

López Sotomayor's side will handle rights, Chilean financing, institutional backing and production in Chile. Pantellisense will take charge of Indian cast and crew, post-production, VFX, newer production technologies, funding and incentives from India, plus distribution in India and the wider South Asian region. The final division of money, creative input and technical work will be fixed in a formal co-production agreement.

The partners also plan to scout locations in Himachal Pradesh's Himalayan region and an Arctic setting alongside Chilean Antarctic locations, and to consult polar and mountain research bodies in both countries. They will share expertise on AI-assisted previsualization, virtual production and post-production, and draw up a joint festival, sales and distribution plan.

Within 90 days, the two sides are due to swap chain-of-title paperwork for the novel and screenplay, along with a development budget and an early financing plan, ahead of a binding agreement setting out each side's financial and creative share as well as territories, credits, revenue splits and rights.

India already has a presence in all three regions the film covers, with research stations Himansh in Himachal Pradesh's Himalayas, Himadri in the Arctic, and Maitri and Bharati in Antarctica.

articles.title: Skydance Products and Publishing Sets Leadership Team Under Josh Silverman
articles.summary: Silverman's team will add oversight of DC Comics, joining existing product and publishing leaders.
articles.content:
Skydance 's products and publishing team has set its executive leadership under Josh Silverman.

Silverman announced the C-suite structure in a memo to staff Monday, which was obtained by The Hollywood Reporter .

Perhaps the most notable change: DC Comics will be a part of the division, with Jim Lee, president, publisher and chief creative officer of DC, and Anne DePies, executive VP and GM of DC, both reporting to Silverman. DC Comics is an incubator for the characters and storylines that ultimately end up on screen.

Mark Kaufman, the executive VP and chief content officer of Warner Bros. Theatre Ventures, will lead that division for Skydance, adapting the company's IP for the stage.

A number of senior Paramount executives will also continue in their roles, including consumer products chief Paul Southern, publishing head Amy Kaplan Jarashow, and head of creative Luis Fernández.

Meanwhile, Robert Oberschelp, who was WBD's head of consumer products, will exit the company.

You can read Silverman's memo below.

Team, Since coming together as Skydance Products & Publishing, we’ve been thoughtfully shaping how we’ll work as one team, bringing together incredible talent and perspective from across our combined organization and positioning ourselves for success and growth. At Skydance, we are building a next-generation media and entertainment company powered by the timeless storytelling of our two iconic studios, accelerated by technology, and built for the future. Products and Publishing is a critically important part of the company’s globally connected ecosystem. Our impact goes beyond individual products, categories and formats. We strengthen and extend the emotional connection between our fans around the world with the brands, franchises, characters and stories they love. Today I'm excited to announce the leadership team that will help guide Skydance Products & Publishing as we build for the future. These talented leaders bring tremendous experience, creativity and passion to our organization, and I’m thrilled to have them by my side as we move forward together. The following leaders will report directly to me, with responsibility for the areas outlined below: Paul Southern, EVP, Consumer Products, will oversee our global consumer products business and retail operations, focusing on expanding our reach, establishing new revenue opportunities, strengthening key partnerships and fostering innovation across our brands and franchises. Paul is a seasoned executive who has led commercialization strategies for some of the world’s most iconic entertainment franchises including long-standing leadership roles at The Walt Disney Company and Lucasfilm. Amy Kaplan Jarashow, SVP, Global Publishing, will oversee our publishing business, including our publishing imprint Skydance Publishing. Under Amy's leadership, publishing will serve as a strategic extension of our content ecosystem, creating new ways for fans to engage with our brands while developing original stories and new intellectual property. Amy brings extensive experience having built her career with some of the industry’s most recognized companies, including Penguin Random House and LEGO. Jim Lee, President, Publisher and Chief Creative Officer, DC, and Anne DePies, EVP and General Manager, DC, will continue to co-lead DC Comics, one of the world’s largest publishers of comics and graphic novels - shaping the future of its iconic characters and enduring stories, and driving the growth and success of the brand across the studio. Mark Kaufman, EVP & Chief Content Officer, Theatre Ventures, will oversee live stage productions across the Skydance portfolio. With leadership roles for 15 years at Warner Bros. and over 15 years at New Line Cinema, Mark has helped develop and produce acclaimed stage productions, worldwide, from Hairspray to The Lost Boys. Luis Fernández, EVP, Creative, will lead the global creative vision, strategy and product development across our portfolio, bringing a consistent, high-quality expression across our properties. With over two decades of experience at The Walt Disney Company and five years leading Consumer Products at Skydance Media, Luis brings a proven track record of building and elevating world-class brands. Melissa Lasdon, SVP, Brand Management & Marketing, will oversee the development of global, long-range, insight-driven brand strategies aligned with the broader organizational priorities while leading marketing efforts to drive growth. She will serve as the central point of coordination across all franchises within our division. Melissa brings extensive experience from The Walt Disney Company, where she held leadership roles spanning Franchise, Brand Marketing, Category Management and Consumer Product Development. Kedar Nadkarni, EVP, CFO & Head of Strategy and Insights, will lead finance for our global businesses while also overseeing strategy, operations and insights, and position the organization for long-term growth. Kedar is an industry veteran whose career includes strategy and finance roles with Disney Consumer Products, The Wall Street Journal, and Deloitte Consulting. Kedar is a dual report to Dennis Cinelli and me. To better connect the international markets with our global business priorities, regional leaders from EMEA, Latin America and APAC will now report directly to Paul Southern and Amy Jarashow to support Consumer Products and Publishing. This structure will create greater alignment, accelerate the sharing of best practices and strengthen our ability to operate as one global and local organization. As part of these organizational changes, Robert Oberschelp will be leaving the company. Robert has been a valued leader whose contributions have left a lasting mark on the business. Please join me in thanking Robert for his many accomplishments and wishing him continued success. We have a clear vision for what we are building and where we are headed. We will create and deliver exceptional products, compelling stories, and meaningful experiences that resonate with audiences around the world. We will remain nimble, curious and entrepreneurial, challenge convention, find new ways to connect with our fans and continually raise the bar for what’s possible. Thank you for the commitment and drive you bring to your work every day. You are what makes this company extraordinary, and what gives me such confidence in our future. We have an exciting road ahead, and I can’t wait to see what we will build together. Josh

The villain of the original Gremlins hasn't appeared in a […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Two years before Gremlins 3 arrives in theaters , Gizmo and Stripe have been reunited for a new Christmas commercial from AT&T. While Gizmo has made several appearances outside of the movies over the years, it's considerably rarer to see Stripe brought to life in live-action. The villain of the original Gremlins hasn't appeared in a theatrical movie since 1984. The new commercial even brings back Stripe in his Mogwai form, complete with his signature white mohawk.

The commercial finds the two Mogwai getting along considerably better than they did in Joe Dante's original movie. The pair are hanging out on a couch playing with Samsung devices with a plate of Christmas cookies in front of them. Fortunately, someone in the house is familiar with the rules of owning a Mogwai and takes the cookies away as the clock strikes midnight. Both characters were brought to life using puppets. It's a particularly welcome sight for fans wondering what the creatures will look like when original Gremlins screenwriter Chris Columbus takes over directing duties for the third movie .

Gremlins Has a Long History of Great Television Commercials Selling products with Mogwai is almost as old as the franchise itself. Kids in the 1980s could start their mornings with a bowl of Gremlins cereal. It's pretty funny in retrospect that a movie featuring a creature exploding in a microwave spawned a breakfast cereal marketed to children. Ralston's commercial for the cereal even incorporated the rules from the movie into its sales pitch. The movie's somewhat complicated relationship with its own merchandising would become one of the many things Dante poked fun at in Gremlins 2: The New Batch .

In 2021, Mountain Dew gave fans something they'd been waiting decades to see when the company reunited Zach Galligan with Gizmo for a commercial promoting Mountain Dew Zero Sugar. The commercial found an older Billy Peltzer still living with Gizmo. Despite having spent decades taking care of the little guy, Billy still hasn't learned his lesson when it comes to letting Gizmo near liquids.

What's fun about the Mountain Dew commercial is that it actually builds on the mythology of the movies. The commercial introduces audiences to Billy's daughter, who has a Mogwai of her own. It even includes an aged-up Gizmo, complete with a white-haired goatee. While commercials featuring characters from beloved movies often recreate scenes from those movies, Mountain Dew essentially produced a 30-second legacy sequel to Gremlins .

Between the Mountain Dew and AT&T commercials, fans have gotten a couple of opportunities to see how well the characters work in live-action more than three decades after the release of Gremlins 2 . Fortunately, neither company felt the need to modernize Gizmo's design or abandon the puppetry that made audiences fall in love with the character in the first place. With Columbus planning to utilize practical creature effects in Gremlins 3 , these commercials might be the best indication yet of what fans can expect to see on the big screen on October 6th, 2028.

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The relationship between toys and comics is, and has always been, a mutually beneficial one. Think of legendary comic writer Larry Hama’s stint on G.I. Joe in the 1980s or Ralph Macchio’s issues for The Transformers . Pairing up toys and comics gives the opportunity to create a broader fictional universe around a pre-existing concept. This either amplifies the love kids already have for a toy, or it gives a toy that isn’t working another chance. It allows the comic to exist beyond pages, giving kids the opportunity to use their own imaginations on what may happen in the fictional worlds created by these writers.

Toys and comics were further intermingled in the 1980s — a great decade for both toys and comics — when several franchises included mini-comics with the release of individual toy figures. Now seen as valuable collectibles, these mini-comics were just bonuses with the toy when they first arrived. Some lines were more successful than others, launching line after line of mini-comics while others stopped after only three issues. See if you can remember any of these beloved toy-comic mashups below!

Although toy giant Mattel acquired it in 1996, Tyco carved out its own niche in the toy market for a time. Tyco was founded in the 1950s as a producer of toy train kits before moving on to pre-built trains, slot cars, and remote control vehicles. In December of 1987, Tyco launched a toy line known as Dino-Riders. With each dinosaur figure released, kids got a mini-comic. Since it was a new toy, Tyco figured a comic would help market the action figures . According to the comic, Dino-Riders was about the battle between the superhuman Valorians and the humanoid Rulons, set during dinosaur times on Earth.

The comic was sixteen pages long, and Tyco would release two issues of it. The second issue continued the narrative from the first one and was included in each box of the toy’s second, third, and Ice-Age series. The mini-issues were written by regular Tyco freelancer Paul Kirchner. In addition to Dino-Riders , Kirchner wrote for Tyco’s Crash Dummies and Spy-Tech toy lines. It would hardly be his only contribution to toy comics, given his work with G.I. Joe, He-Man, Thundercats, and Power Rangers in the 1980s and 1990s.

Before the company filed for bankruptcy and had its products bought out by Hasbro in 1989, Coleco Industries, known for Cabbage Patch Dolls, created a line of action figures. These figures were known as the Sectaurs , the warriors of Symbion. The warriors of Symbion were humanoids who had insect- and arachnid-like features.

The Sectaurs toys included nine mini-comics with the series released in 1984. From 1985 to 1986, a series of regular comics from Marvel about the Sectaurs was written by Bill Mantlo. Mantlo is perhaps better known for his work on the Micronauts and Rom , along with co-creating Rocket Raccoon and the pair Cloak and Dagger. While each toy’s mini-comic was meant to spotlight the character or playset it came with, some comics were more common than others, such as “The World of Symbion”.

MASK had three mini-comics that came out with the Kenner toys. The comics were randomly included in 1985’s series one boxes, and they were the first comics that were produced for MASK. These comics delved into the world set up by the animated series but brought the characterization, history, and worldbuilding beyond it. The first comic gave MASK a beginning, something that was never given attention in the animated series, while the two other issues told comic-exclusive adventures.

“Flaming Beginnings” had a double storyline, showing the beginning of Matt Tracker’s battle with Mayhem and how he lost his brother Andy, along with present-day Miles Mayhem’s attempt to use a human robot to sabotage Matt Tracker and Bruce Sato. “Monster from VENOM” featured another attack on Matt Trakker and Bruce Sato, this time featuring a Loch Ness Monster-esque creature, while “Assault on Boulder Hill” concluded the saga with yet another of Miles Mayhem’s plans going awry.

Masters of the Universe was a force to be reckoned with during the 1980s. Unlike the other entries on this list, Masters of the Universe as a brand only dates back to 1982. Its parent company, Mattel , had created it to re-establish a foothold in the boys’ toy market, having already conquered the girls’ with Barbie. Given that the line was new, the Masters of the Universe action figures came with a mini-comic meant to introduce not only the individual toy’s character but also the larger lore around Eternia.

In the US, there was a plethora of Masters of the Universe comics, released from 1982 to 1987 across seven series rollouts. The comics predated the animated series, but the comic line would adjust starting in 1984 when there was a larger canon to contend with. DC Comics would take over production of the comics starting in 1983, with writer Gary Cohn taking over from Donald F. Glut.

From 1984 to 1985, the Super Powers collection from Kenner Toys published 23 mini-comics. These mini-comics included fan-favorite heroes such as Superman, Batman, and Wonder Woman going up against the formidable Joker, Brainiac, and Lex Luthor. The second series focused on a broader base of heroes — Green Arrow, Dr. Fate, Firestorm, Martian Manhunter — than DC’s Trinity or Robin.

The Kenner toy line gave a big push for Jack Kirby’s “Fourth World”. Kirby’s “Fourth World” refers to Darkseid and his minions, characters that are instrumental in the DC Universe today. Kenner reached out to Kirby directly and had him commission designs for the action figures, such as Darkseid. A similar decision was made with George Perez when Kenner asked him to create a design for Cyborg.

While Super Powers started out as a toyline, it branched out into books, games, puzzles, toys, and was cross-branded with the Super Friends tv show. The mini-comics existed largely out of continuity, but Crisis on Infinite Earths: The Compendium classified the Super Powers world as Earth Thirty-Two. 

Which action figure mini-comics came as a surprise? Which were a no-brainer? Let us know in the comments below!

articles.title: You Can See Everything Is Hitting Box Office Milestones, But It’s Not Gonna Beat Out Michael Jackson (Hee Hee)
articles.summary: The documentary has been making tons of headlines.
articles.content:
The buzziest film on the 2026 movie schedule has to be You Can See Everything, and it just hit a major milestone by crossing the $100 million mark at the box office. For a movie that was made for a reported $7 million, it’s certainly one of the most successful A24 releases ever, but the Elizabeth Holmes documentary is nowhere close to the top-grossing documentary of all time, worldwide. That record belongs to the King of Pop himself for the posthumously released Michael Jackson : This Is It from 2009. How does it stack up to other documentaries? Well, it depends on how you count things.

You Can See Everything wasn’t quite the rocket ship that Fahrenheit 9/11 was out of the box, but it did a ton of steady business for weeks, finally topping the weekend box office in its third week of release . Now, after its release in the United Kingdom, the Nathan Fielder/Lance Oppenheim-directed documentary has joined rarefied air as a documentary hitting that milestone. The $100 million mark slots You Can See Everyone into 7th worldwide.

That means the only two non-music and non-nature documentaries in the top ten are Fahrenheit 9/11 and You Can See Everything . It also means that You Can See Everything won’t be catching up to Michael Jackson. I don’t expect You Can See Everything to improve significantly at the worldwide box office. Elizabeth Holmes may be fascinating and infamous here, but Jackson was a massive star in every corner of the globe. In fact, domestically, This Is It actually trails You Can See Everything by almost $20 million.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Death is one of the few constants in life. Given how it's an unavoidable part of existence, it's no surprise that there's an endless number of works exploring all the different ways it can manifest. The newest upcoming project from Ignition Press is set to add to those numbers in a unique way , imagining a post-apocalyptic world where death has disastrous consequences. Dying has become the leading cause of death for everyone else left alive, and the drive to stay alive for the people who make life worth living is the main force pushing Pilgrimage Through Monsterland forward. This new comic follows a group of survivors as they trek their way across a ruined America, with survival being challenged in ways they couldn't have imagined.

Newbery Honor and Nebula Award-winning Lipan Apache writer Darcie Little Badger ( Elatsoe , Children of Owl ) is joined by incredible artist Kelsey Ramsay ( Dark Spaces: Good Deeds , Godzilla: Heist ) in crafting a story all about nature, death, and the love that pushes us to keep going. This story will have a major focus on the evolving dynamic between people and the world we live in, exploring the sprawling country through an Indigenous point of view, all while our protagonist tries to survive both the world and a serial killer. Pilgrimage Through Monsterland #1 hits store shelves on May 5, 2027, and ComicBook is honored to announce it all right here.

The main character, Nat, was an ordinary accountant living in LA when a curse befell humanity. Now, at the moment of death, corpses would transform into something entirely different. The lucky ones turned to stone, but others would mutate into horrible monsters, and some even unleashed devastating tornadoes, or something even worse. Wanting nothing more than to learn the fate of her sister, the last family she has left, Nat joined a group of survivors making their way to Texas. Between an entirely too enthusiastic guide, a group of familiar faces and strangers, monsters that stalk their steps, scavengers, and unnatural disasters, Nat learns that her problems are only just beginning, as she starts to think that one of her own is a murderer.

“ Pilgrimage Through Monsterland is the dark fantasy adventure I've always wanted to write,” said writer Darcie Little Badger. “What if death became a moment of transformation, unleashing tornadoes, monsters, and fire? How'd the world respond to this sudden, cataclysmic change in reality? The premise is Weird, but the core story is universal: at its heart, Pilgrimage Through Monsterland is about the lengths people go for family and survival. A group of strangers must rely on each other as they trek across a scarred and dangerous country, and Nat must trust that there's a home waiting for her on the other side…assuming she survives. Which, as the journey progresses, becomes increasingly unlikely. It's a professional dream to work with Kelsey, whose art captures the humanity of characters (and the horror of monsters and apocalyptic hellscapes). I'm so excited to see this project come to life.”

“ Pilgrimage Through Monsterland is such a meaningful project, giving a voice to stories untold, and it's a real honor to be involved,” said artist Kelsey Ramsay. “Darcie has managed to make every character feel so distinct, layered and complex, which has made bringing them to life on the page such a joy. I hope readers can recognize something of themselves in these characters and connect with the variety of people and personalities throughout the story. But, of course, I also hope they have an awesome time enjoying all the action, adventure and monster craziness along the way!”

This series is definitely a passionate project for Darcie Little Badger. Although she was born in Minnesota, she considers Texas her home, and her work in the Indigenous Futurisms movement always elevates her writing to the next level. This comic promises to bring a very unique perspective to the concept of death and our relationship with the world, drawing on Indigenous legends to tell a tale that's as invigorating as it is horrifying. This story will explore death in all its forms, and with the very idea of grief and despair being baked into the story's main threat, it's guaranteed to be a joy to read through.

Alongside Darcie Little Badger on the script and Kelsey Ramsay on the inks, the team is made up of colorist Tríona Farrell ( Showdown , Gotham City Sirens ) and letterer Ariana Maher ( Justice League Unlimited , Superman ). Additional details about Pilgrimage Through Monsterland will be released in early 2027, but be sure to guarantee you can snag your copy of the first issue at your local comic shop by pre-ordering before April 12, 2027.

Pilgrimage Through Monsterland releases on May 5, 2027!

It’s kind of hard to believe that Vanna White has been co-hosting Wheel of Fortune for nearly 45 years as of the 2026 television schedule . In a recent appearance on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon , White told the story of her audition, why she was chosen by legendary producer Merv Griffin, and even what her first puzzle was (and the first letter she turned).

I mean, yeah, fair enough, right? Though White’s role on the show has grown a lot over the years, far beyond only turning (now touching) the letters (and working hard for her salary ). No one can argue with Griffin’s logic, and almost five incredible decades later, it's clear he couldn’t have made a better choice.

George, it should be noted, was not a biological uncle, but was a close friend of her mother’s. On her first day filming, however, she was still quite nervous (and was even worried it wouldn't work out in the early days ), telling Fallon:

Famously, that wasn't the first time appearing on a game show. Two years before getting the job, she appeared as a contestant on The Price Is Right . It includes Belgian-American actress, writer and director Bérangère McNeese, who spent part of her childhood in Kentucky and draws on both American and French comedy traditions; Daniel, best known for her Instagram character series “Les Caractères” and Canal+’s “Chamouxland”; Sawsan Abès, whose credits include “Ourika” and who is set to appear in the next season of “The White Lotus”; Emma Ebouaney, who’s built a following with her offbeat YouTube parodies, spoof reports and retro-inspired sketches; Bertrand Goncalves, who appeared in “Camembert” and Canal+’s “Super Plan,” hosted by Antoine de Caunes; François de Brauer, a theater performer known for his character-driven one-man shows, including “La Loi des prodiges”; and Luca Besse, whose credits include “Terrible Jungle.”

Eric Hannezo, head of programming, creative and development at Mediawan France and president of Black Dynamite and Mediawan Sport, pointed out that “comedy has long been part of our DNA.”

Hannezo previously produced “Le Débarquement,” an “SNL”-inspired sketch comedy show spearheaded by Jean Dujardin, Guillaume Canet and Gilles Lellouche, which aired two specials on Canal+ in 2013 and featured stars such as Marion Cotillard, as well as Alex Lutz and Payet himself.

The French launch comes amid renewed international momentum for the franchise. “Saturday Night Live UK,” now in its second season on Sky, drew 3.1 million views and more than 570 million social video views during its first season, according to NBCUniversal.

articles.title: OG Christmas Vacation Director Gets Real About How Feud With Chevy Chase Made Him Quit The Film
articles.summary: Chris Columbus needed the job, but not badly enough to work with Chevy Chase.
articles.content:
Chris Columbus directed Home Alone , but he came remarkably close to spending Christmas with the Griswolds instead. Before that movie became a holiday staple, he was supposed to direct National Lampoon's Christmas Vacation . Then he met Chevy Chase, and Columbus' latest account makes his decision to walk away sound even gutsier than I realized.

Columbus was coming off 1988's Heartbreak Hotel , which left him convinced his directing career might be over. He'd returned to Chicago and was staying with his in-laws when John Hughes called . The Christmas Vacation offer was supposed to get him back behind the camera, and he'd already started shooting second-unit footage.

The filmmaker has spoken harshly about Chase before . But this time, he said he's less interested in adding to the actor's bad press . Then he recalled how things reached the point where he called Hughes and quit:

I appreciate that Columbus is making room for a little perspective here. He didn't suddenly declare the feud resolved or pretend the experience was pleasant. He just sounds tired of spending another interview beating up Chase. Fair enough. I'd be tired of telling that story, too, especially knowing it started with a job he desperately needed. But the Harry Potter franchise filmmaker continued:

Jeremiah S. Chechik took over Christmas Vacation , and Home Alone arrived in theaters in 1990. I'm grateful both movies became Christmas classics , although it's amusing to imagine what Columbus might have done with Clark Griswold's disastrous holiday lighting display. Given those early meetings, I suspect he'd rather not imagine it at all.

articles.title: Star Trek Once Reused a Monster From Another Classic Sci-Fi Series & Almost Nobody Noticed
articles.summary: The aliens of Star Trek had to look convincing to viewers on a reasonably low budget before the franchise became one of the most popular and successful sci-fi franchises on TV. This meant a fair bit of ingenuity when it came to costumes, makeup, and utilizing whatever the studio could use. Which, as it turns […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The aliens of Star Trek had to look convincing to viewers on a reasonably low budget before the franchise became one of the most popular and successful sci-fi franchises on TV. This meant a fair bit of ingenuity when it came to costumes, makeup, and utilizing whatever the studio could use. Which, as it turns out, included more than a little inspiration from another sci-fi show.

A strange yet fascinating example occurred when an alien life form from another TV show helped inspire a creature encountered by the crew of the U.S.S. Enterprise. The most surprising thing about this reference is that it wasn't simply a case of one alien looking similar to another. In fact, one talented creature performer used his craftsmanship to create practical aliens while helping keep production costs down. It's one of those revelations that becomes even more interesting when you consider how much old sci-fi TV regularly borrowed from one another.

The link can be traced back to The Outer Limits , which played host to scores of strange life-forms during its 1963 to 1965 run. One of these was encountered in the 1965 episode "The Probe." This creature was a giant alien microbe brought to life by stuntman, actor, and creature designer Janos Prohaska. And this is where it gets a bit more complicated. Prohaska would later bring his creature-making skills to Star Trek , designing and wearing the costume of one of the franchise's strangest aliens. Who would have thought a monster from another great sci-fi TV series would help inspire one of Star Trek 's most iconic encounters?

That fiend was the Horta in "The Devil in the Dark." Prohaska constructed and performed in the suit himself, and demonstrated the creature's movements for producer Gene L. Coon, helping inspire the episode's story. No, the connection isn't simply that the original Outer Limits costume was dragged over to the Enterprise without any changes. Rather, Prohaska modified his earlier giant microbe costume, adding details such as veins and a fringe to create the Horta's distinctive appearance. Pretty clever bit of sci-fi TV trivia, if you think about it. The very same guy who helped bring one weird alien to life on The Outer Limits went on to bring us another one on Star Trek . And if you've ever wondered how Star Trek came up with so many wonderfully bizarre monsters in the '60s, there you go: it all came down, in part, to one talented creature performer and one very unusual costume.

Of course, Star Trek was not the only sci-fi show in town. TV budgets in the 1960s were not unlimited, and not every episode warranted a new alien costume or piece of makeup. Borrowing an existing costume or appliance was a reasonable fix. This was especially true considering that some of the same creative people worked on both shows. Makeup artist Fred Phillips worked on both productions, supervising makeup for The Outer Limits before taking on the same role for Star Trek . His involvement in both series is another example of how closely connected these classic television productions could be.

And the Anthropoid Ape wasn't the only Star Trek creature with a connection to The Outer Limits . The humanoid bird seen in "The Cage" has a particularly interesting connection to the Megasoid from "The Duplicate Man." The costume is believed to have been reused for the Star Trek creature, although some details were changed. The Anthropoid Ape from the same pilot also had a connection to The Outer Limits : its facial piece had previously appeared on the Calco creature in the episode "Fun and Games," paired with a different furry costume. It's another fun example of how these classic sci-fi productions shared more than just a love of strange-looking aliens. Sometimes, a monster could find a second life on an entirely different television show. Not a bad career move for a creature from the 1960s.

This took quite a bit of digging, and there are plenty of sources and behind-the-scenes details on the subject. If I missed something or you have another interesting detail to add, let me know! Now, join the away team in the comments: Did you know about this Star Trek connection, and what other recycled creatures or props have you spotted across the franchise? Let's hear it!

An ITN spokeswoman said: "ITN does not use NDAs to prevent people talking openly about their experiences with the company, including at Channel 4 News. We stopped using confidentiality clauses in settlement agreements in 2022, and also lifted them from the small number of people who had previously been subject to them. We have listened and learned, and apologised where we have got things wrong in the past."

Discussion about NDAs has returned to the fore in UK entertainment after Russell Brand was sentence to 10 years in prison for rape and sexual assault and allegations about David Walliams were published by The Guardian and ITN-operated ITV News, allegations that Walliams vehemently denies. Both celebrities were reported to have used NDAs, prompting British ministers to look into ways they can quickly change the law to expand protections that stop NDAs being used to cover up harassment or discrimination. These protections are being implemented via the new Employment Rights Act.

The UK's influential Digital, Culture, Media & Sport Committee has annonced a high-profile probe into industry NDA use, with evidence sessions set to begin in two weeks. Witnesses and timings will be announced shortly and it feels highly likely that executives from ITN or Channel 4 will be invited to speak. Separately, Channel 4, where Brand used to host shows, has been under pressure for historic NDA use, with CEO Priya Dogra telling the committee last week that the network uses confidentality clauses in a limited way with “pretty large caveats." articles.title: The Punisher Just Made the Ultimate Argument Against Spider-Man's No-Kill Rule

While that is the go-to argument for killing villains, Spider-Man has the same code in Marvel Comics. That same argument was brought up in a new comic where the Punisher told Spider-Man why his […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Everyone loves to talk about Batman's no-kill rule and how it always results in villains coming back to kill more people. While that is the go-to argument for killing villains, Spider-Man has the same code in Marvel Comics. That same argument was brought up in a new comic where the Punisher told Spider-Man why his refusal to kill villains will always come back to haunt him. The series is Punisher vs. The Amazing Spider-Man , and it had Spider-Man and the Punisher reluctantly teaming up, with each hero believing he could convince the other that his way was better. That all came to a head in the final issue of the miniseries.

In Punisher vs. The Amazing Spider-Man #5 (2026) by Dan Abnett and Alvaro Lopez, the Punisher learned that the woman he was working with, Smokeshow, was a villain and was using him all along. With the Punisher gunning to bring her down, Spider-Man rushed into action to stop him. In the end, the Punisher called out Spider-Man for claiming to want to save everyone while allowing all his villains to live, which puts everyone in danger.

Smokeshow was shocked when she saw that the Punisher was gunning for her, and she didn't understand why at first, until she realized Frank Castle had discovered the truth. This was the ultimate betrayal for Frank since he served with Smokeshow in the Marines, and he thought she was helping him get rid of drug cartels, but she was really clearing out the competition and was leading her own cartel as well. The Punisher was rushing in, with the intent of killing everyone. That is when Spider-Man showed up to stop him.

This led to Spider-Man fighting the Punisher , even as he gunned his way through the office building, trying to reach Smokeshow. It started when Spider-Man webbed the gun out of Frank's hand before he could execute a man. Spider-Man said no one dies, and the Punisher opened fire on Spider-Man before racing up the stairs. This eventually led to Spider-Man reaching Smokeshow first, and he saved her by webbing the Punisher before he could kill her, although he was too late to stop Frank from killing Smokeshow's main enforcer. When Frank killed the man, Spider-Man knocked Frank out for the count.

This is what then led to their big conversation about what makes the two men different. Spider-Man said he made a big mistake by believing that he could trust the Punisher. He then said things weren't funny anymore, and he told Smokeshow to turn herself in. Then he told the Punisher he was going to jail too and apologized for not being able to help him. That made Frank say Spider-Man couldn't because he was just being Spider-Man and Frank was being the Punisher. They were never a good fit. He then said Spider-Man would lose every time he got in a fight with a villain.

This led to the argument that when a hero like Batman or Spider-Man allows the villains to live and sends them to jail every time, they would always come back to hurt them. When Spider-Man said he would never kill, the Punisher said that meant he lost every time. He said Spider-Man will beat the villains, and they will get up again. He said if Spider-Man were serious, he would see that he was never stopping the villains from hurting anyone else. To make his point, Frank said Spider-Man should kill him.

This shocked Spider-Man, but the Punisher pressed on. He said jail won't stop him, and if Spider-Man doesn't kill him, the Punisher will always be back, "just like every freak in your costume-parade life." Spider-Man asked if it was a threat, and the Punisher said it was just a "statement of fact." The Punisher said that Spider-Man would risk his life to stop the villains and then let them live, and they would always come back for more. The Punisher said that he would come back for more.

Spider-Man then said that Frank was smart and rational, and he doesn't understand why Frank doesn't get it. The Punisher responded bluntly that he is smart and rational and that "friendly" will only get Spider-Man so far. While the Punisher is right, Spider-Man is also a man of strong morals, so this was never going to work. That said, it was also a case of Spider-Man likely knowing that the Punisher was going to escape, since he had given Frank some web solvent earlier, Frank escaped, saying that Spider-Man would never finish what he started. On the other hand, the Punisher said he would finish what Spider-Man can't.

What are your thoughts on the Punisher vs. The Amazon Spider-Man series ? Let us know your thoughts on the Punisher's description of Spider-Man in the comments below.
